caption: What if you shrank to the size of an ant? At about 5 mm tall, falling off a tower stops being scary: a falling ant only reaches about 6 km/h, so tiny creatures can walk away from huge falls. Rain is a different story. Each drop becomes a boulder, yet mosquitoes get hit by raindrops up to 50 times their weight and survive by going with the flow. The real danger is water itself, because at that size surface tension grabs you like glue. Your new neighbours are tough: many ants carry 10 to 50 times their own body weight. And there are a lot of them, about 20 quadrillion ants on Earth, roughly 2.5 million for every human. Together they outweigh all wild birds and mammals combined. Plot twist: in Odisha's Mayurbhanj, red weaver ants are made into Similipal kai chutney, which got a GI tag in 2024. Would YOU shrink to ant size for a day? 👇
